text.p: French building materials group Lafarge underperformed the stock market on Tuesday ahead of 1996 results publication on Wednesday which analysts believe will come in lower than in 1995.
The share was down 2.21 percent at 1504 GMT at 371.0 francs, while the CAC-40 leading share index was down 0.33 percent.
One analyst said the expectation was for a net attributable profit of 1.9-2.0 billion this time round, after 2.350 billion in 1995. "Some take a bid view of this drop," he said.
Another expert said the results were hard to predict because of the various possibilities for treating exceptionals and financial charges.

"The company made a lot of investment in 1996, between six and seven billion francs. Did this come from cashflow or bank credit? What will the impact be on debt and financial charges," said the expert.

He nonetheless said he remained positive on the group, saying investments in cement, plaster and concrete in Britain, Germany and Poland were good opportunities which could pay off when the economic climate improved.
